non_haematological_toxicity_grade.label: Other clinically relevant non-haematological toxicity grade

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate; intervention may be indicated and instrumental activities may be limited.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe or medically significant; hospital care may be indicated and self-care may be limited.

non_haematological_toxicity_grade.assessment_guidance: Grade using the applicable CTCAE term, objective findings, intervention required and functional impact.

hypersensitivity.label: Known hypersensitivity to a regimen component

diarrhoea_grade.label: Diarrhoea grade

options.label: Grade 0 — No toxicity
options.description: No increase above the patient's usual stool frequency or ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Increase of fewer than 4 stools per day above baseline, or mild increase in ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Increase of 4–6 stools per day above baseline, or moderate increase in ostomy output; limits instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Increase of 7 or more stools per day above baseline, incontinence, hospital care indicated, or severe ostomy-output increase; limits self-care activities of daily living.

diarrhoea_grade.assessment_guidance: Grade using increase in stools over baseline, ostomy output, need for hospitalisation and impact on self-care; do not grade from the word “diarrhoea” alone.

mucositis_grade.label: Oral mucositis/stomatitis grade

options.label: Grade 1 — Mild
options.description: Asymptomatic or mild symptoms; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2 — Moderate
options.description: Moderate pain or ulceration that does not interfere with oral intake; modified diet indicated.

options.label: Grade 3 — Severe
options.description: Severe pain that interferes with oral intake.

mucositis_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess pain, ulceration and whether oral intake is preserved, modified or impossible.

renal_input.reason: The NCCP mitomycin pathway uses CrCl thresholds at 10 mL/min and a high-dose caution range of 10–60 mL/min.

renal_impairment_severity.label: Clinical renal impairment category for fluorouracil
renal_impairment_severity.help: The NCCP source advises considering fluorouracil dose reduction only in severe renal impairment and cautions that renal impairment can affect uracil-based DPD phenotyping.

hepatic_impairment_severity.label: Clinical hepatic impairment category for fluorouracil
hepatic_impairment_severity.help: Use the clinically established hepatic impairment category in addition to the absolute bilirubin and AST thresholds in the NCCP table.

dose_modifications: Source-reconciled component-specific haematological, renal, hepatic, DPD and diarrhoea/mucositis pathways are encoded as independently actionable rules.
Absolute bilirubin and AST thresholds are retained for fluorouracil; AST ×ULN is calculated from the local laboratory profile for the mitomycin hepatic review pathway.
The current official NCCP PDF remains the prescribing source and all dose modifications require Consultant review.
monitoring: FBC, renal profile and liver profile at baseline
FBC, renal profile and liver profile weekly throughout treatment
DPD testing before first fluorouracil unless previously tested; interpret uracil phenotype cautiously in moderate/severe renal impairment
